title: Ghana Revenue Authority launches Publican AI trade analytics, which may have recovered GH¢15 million
summary: GRA's Publican AI customs analytics, supplied by an unnamed Cyprus-based firm, rolled out from 1 February 2026 at Tema Port; the OECD AI Incidents Monitor summary says GH¢15 million was recovered, ...
account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI, a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation, and states that the system has already recovered GH¢15 million from fraudulent importers, sourcing a GhanaWeb story titled 'Government recovers GH¢15 million through new trade data system'; the entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong saying that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment, that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours, that pilots showed 40-45% revenue gains, and that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026; that article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm. The date used is the AIM entry date.
purpose: Identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation and give full coverage of customs assessment.
developer: A Cyprus-based firm, unnamed in the fetched article
taxonomy_note: Tax yield is read as the authority's revenue; Trustible's description is written for product sales.

ratings.reason: The recovery figure is a secondary summary and the revenue gain is a projection; no verified outcome for the GRA is documented.
Public revenue effects are projected, not observed, in the fetched sources.

ai_role.statement: Neither source describes how the analytics identify undervaluation or what share of the claimed recovery the system produced; the system is vendor-built and deployed by the GRA.

evidence.citation: OECD AI Incidents Monitor, entry 2026-01-16-e77d, classified AI Incident
evidence.title: Ghana Deploys AI System to Combat Customs Fraud and Recover Revenue
